data.narrative:
Vinci is an AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage, founded by Hardik Kabaria, Sarah Osentoski, and Vincent Rerolle. The broader AI & Software sector contains 12 known peers, comprised of 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private firms including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. However, the peer set lacks sufficient depth for conventional median-based valuation work.

A peer-median approach is not applicable here. Screening the 12 same-sector comparables for matching stage, adjacent-stage positioning, or similar valuation tiers yielded zero datapoints meeting the minimum threshold of three observations. The absence of same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier peers within the narrow AI & Software universe prevents reliable triangulation via this method. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce significant bias given the heterogeneity of business models, revenue scales, and growth trajectories across the broader cohort.

Without sufficient narrow-set peer data to anchor valuation, alternative methods—such as discounted cash flow analysis, comparable transaction multiples, or explicit venture round benchmarking—would be required to establish a defensible range. The primary constraint is data sparsity at Vinci's specific stage and positioning within AI & Software, not absence of sector-level comparables. Any valuation conclusion must remain conditional pending disclosure of stage, financials, or additional comparable transactions at similar funding rounds.
